claims.claim_text: Indexed Robert L Van Nice is confirmed as architect Robert Lawrence Van Nice, who served in OSS X-2 in London and Bern in 1944-1945.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional finding aid gives his full name, architectural career, exact OSS branch, offices and service years.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an authoritative collection-level biography based partly on his official OSS dossier.
claims.temporal_assessment: The same chronology documents his prewar work and later OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The indexed spelling remains primary; the full name is retained as a documented variant.

claims.claim_text: Before his 1944 OSS X-2 service, Robert Lawrence Van Nice worked on William Emerson's independently run architectural survey of Hagia Sophia.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The finding aid says Emerson hired him in 1937; Dumbarton Oaks states that Cambridge drawing work preceded his London and Bern OSS work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed exact-name, career and OSS dossier chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded immediate civilian work; the exact 1944 transition day is not stated.
claims.match_notes: The project—not MIT, the Byzantine Institute or postwar Dumbarton Oaks—is the historically supported affiliation.

claims.claim_text: Robert Lawrence Van Nice's last documented civilian work before OSS was architectural surveying and drawing for the Hagia Sophia project sponsored by William Emerson.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional chronology runs from Emerson's 1937 hiring through wartime Cambridge drawings and then to OSS service in 1944.
claims.temporal_assessment: Last documented civilian work before OSS; no intervening employer is identified.
claims.match_notes: Reported separately from his immediate-affiliation claim so the two research questions remain auditable.

claims.claim_text: From October 1936 through July 1937, Robert Lawrence Van Nice worked under architect and archaeologist Myron Bement Smith on surveys in Iran.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The finding aid dates the Iran work and describes his measurements and drawings at Isfahan, Shiraz and Ashtarjan.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed exact-name and continuous architectural-career evidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly documented prewar work, preceding the Hagia Sophia project.
claims.match_notes: Kept as earlier employment rather than being presented as the immediate OSS predecessor.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Samuel Van Valkenber is high-confidence matched to Clark University geographer Samuel Van Valkenburg, who worked at OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Clark's institutional article explicitly joins the professor's name, Clark role and OSS service; the index surname is visibly clipped at the table boundary.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from rare-name expansion, university role and explicit OSS context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Clark sources document his faculty career before and after wartime service.
claims.match_notes: The printed truncated form remains recoverable and the documented full spelling is a variant.

claims.claim_text: Samuel Van Valkenburg was a Clark University geography professor before his wartime OSS work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Clark records his permanent appointment from 1932, active teaching and research in 1941, and later identifies him as an OSS veteran.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence rare-name, institutional-role and explicit OSS match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Clark is the last documented civilian employer; the exact OSS start and any intervening government assignment remain unresolved.
claims.match_notes: Not labeled an explicit direct transfer; wartime Quartermaster consulting is later and remains a separate chronology question.
